title: Reductions Taken for the Way a Policyholder Pays Their Supplement Premium
content:
A reduction may be taken from the monthly premium the household discount leaves on a policy under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies, according to what the premium account shows about the way the policyholder pays. The reduction is settled as follows.

| What the account and the policy record show | The reduction taken |
|---|---|
| A payment covering 12 months of cover stands on the account, and a payment that settled a billing period in full stands within the 12 months to date | The plan letter's annual payment discount, taken on the monthly premium the household discount leaves |
| No payment covering 12 months of cover stands on the account, the premium is drawn by bank transfer, and at least 2 payments that settled a billing period in full stand within the 12 months to date | The plan letter's flat bank transfer reduction, for each month of the span |
| None of those holds | No reduction is taken |

### How the rows differ

The first row turns on a single payment on the account that covered 12 months of cover, together with at least one payment that settled a billing period in full within the 12 months to date. Its reduction is a percentage, taken on the monthly premium the household discount leaves.

The second row is reached only where no payment covering 12 months of cover stands on the account. It then requires all three of its limbs: no such payment, premium drawn by bank transfer, and at least 2 payments within the 12 months to date that each settled a billing period in full. Its reduction is not a percentage but the plan letter's flat amount, taken for each month of the span.

One payment that settled a billing period in full within the 12 months to date is enough for the first row; 2 are needed for the second.

### Hypothetical figures

On Ridgecrest Medicare Supplement Plan G, where a payment covering 12 months of cover stands on the account and one payment within the 12 months to date settled a billing period in full, the reduction is that plan letter's annual payment discount of 6 per cent taken on the monthly premium the household discount leaves.

On Ridgecrest Medicare Supplement Plan A, where no payment on the account covered 12 months of cover, the premium is drawn by bank transfer and 3 payments within the 12 months to date each settled a billing period in full, the reduction is that plan letter's flat bank transfer reduction of 1.50 for each month of the span.

Where the premium is drawn by bank transfer but only 1 payment within the 12 months to date settled a billing period in full, and no payment covered 12 months of cover, no reduction is taken.
